tronic devices can link a kitchen scale used to weigh food eaten directly 
to a computer, making recording of portion sizes more accurate.
Mobile devices can be used to photograph meals and document portion 
sizes. This process can either be active (i.e., the user takes an image be-
fore and after a meal) or passive (i.e., a wearable camera takes images 
during daily activities, including mealtime). These options can assist with 
more accurate reporting of intake, which previously relied completely on 
recall. However, if images are not of satisfactory quality, or if they do not 
provide a reference point to judge portion size, they may underestimate 
intake (Gemming et al, 2015). Other apps use a bar code reader to trans-
mit data from food labels to a food record (Six et al, 2011; Thompson et al, 
2010; Some of the popular apps are:
